26.0.0.en: 1 Blessed is the husband of a good wife, and the number of his days is doubled. 2 A virtuous woman delights her husband, and makes him spend his years in peace. 3 A good wife is a good portion, given as a lot to him who fears the Lord, 4 so that his heart is glad, and his face cheerful at all times, whether he be rich or poor.

26.0.1.en: Happy is the husband of a good wife, for the number of his days is doubled [1].

26.0.2.en: A good wife gives her husband happiness [1, 2, 4], long life [1] and peace [2]. The holy family that enjoys the peace of God has an effect even upon a person's physical and psychological health. On the contrary, the existence of family disputes, especially between the spouses, shatters the psychology of the husband, wife and children, and affects their bodily health. The wise man says: "A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband: but she that maketh ashamed is as rottenness in his bones" (Prov 12:4).

26.0.3.en: From the spiritual side, the doubling of the number of a person's days means the doubling of blessing. A person may live to old age, yet his days are counted as nothing, and a child may die and his few days be counted in the eyes of God and the eyes of the heavenly ones better than thousands of years. What the unborn John the Baptist did, while he was not yet complete and had not yet come out into the world, was greater than the works of the high priests and all the leaders at that time. Moreover, on the great day of the Lord we shall be surprised by little children who are counted great heroes, whose days are counted exceedingly long and fruitful in the Lord. It was said of God's godly people such as Abraham, Isaac and Job that they died full of days (Gen 25:8; 35:23).

26.0.4.en: v How can we express the marital happiness which the Church joins together, which the oblation confirms, and which the blessing seals? [1]

26.1.0.en: Tertullian A virtuous wife delights her husband, and he spends his years filled with peace [2].

26.1.1.en: Where there is godliness together with sincerity, family life is transformed into a life almost heavenly, and the family tastes blessing in every work to which their hands are extended, and the joy of the Spirit comes upon them all, and they are filled with inner peace.

26.1.2.en: If heaven in its essence is a "fellowship of love" and a "life of unity in God, the center of heaven," then true married life in the very core of its being is a unity of marital love, through which the two become one.

26.1.3.en: v Marriage is greater than being merely human; it is a miniature kingdom, a little house of the Lord.

26.2.0.en: St. Clement of Alexandria A good wife is a great portion, and she is the portion of him who fears the Lord [3].

26.2.1.en: The God-fearing husband looks to his good wife and counts her a divine gift. The Lord presented her to him as a great portion in which he delights. Where there is mutual love between God and the godly man, the believer says: "I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine" (Song 6:3). The believer counts the Lord as his portion (Jer 3:24). And the Lord counts His children as His portion, as was said of the tribe of Levi: "The Lord is his inheritance" (Deut 10:9). Thus the husband counts his wife his great portion, and the wife counts her husband her great portion.

26.2.2.en: v I do not reject the bond of marriage; rather, I submit to it in a greater love, for by this I bear witness, confessing, to my wife whom the Lord appointed for me, and I honor her, and I do not refuse to be joined to her by the bond of love in Christ, which is never loosed [2].

26.2.3.en: Abba Theonas A good heart, in rich or poor, is a cheerful face at all times [3] [4].

26.3.0.en: The bishop and monk St. Ambrose speaks of the married man in his relation to his wife, saying: [A man without a wife is reckoned like one who has no house [4].]

26.3.1.en: v There is nothing more precious, and nothing more precious can be found, than that a person be loved by his wife and love her!

26.3.2.en: Scripture says: "A wife who agrees with her husband" (as one of the three blessings that the wise man mentioned) (see Sir 25:1), because where this (love) exists there is wealth and prosperity overflows, and where it is absent nothing else avails, but all things go in the wrong way, and life becomes misery and anxiety.

26.3.3.en: Let us seek this before everything! He who seeks money seeks nothing. Seek what endures!

26.3.4.en: Do not seek a wife from among the rich, lest the increase of wealth on her side cause arrogance.

26.4.0.en: It befits us not to seek a wife for her wealth, but to seek her as a partner for us in life, for the sake of management, to be a helper for the bearing of children. God gave the woman not to bring money but to be a helper! [5]

26.5.0.en: 5 Three things my heart fears, and for the fourth I made supplication with my face: 6 the slander of a city, the gathering of a mob, 7 and a false accusation. All this is heavier than death. 8 But a woman jealous of a woman is heartache and mourning, 9 and her tongue is a whip that strikes everyone. 10 A wicked wife is a chafing yoke, and he who takes hold of her is like one who grasps a scorpion. 11 A drunken woman is a great wrath, and her shame is not covered. 12 The adultery of a woman is in the lifting up of her eyes, and it is known by her eyelids. 13 Keep a strict watch on the daughter who has little shame, lest she find an opportunity and give herself away. 14 Beware of her impudent eye, and do not wonder if she transgresses against you. 15 She opens her mouth like a thirsty traveler, and drinks from every water that she comes upon, and sits down at every tent peg, and opens her quiver to every arrow.

26.6.0.en: Among the evil traits of the wife are: jealousy of her rival [6], a biting tongue [6], drunkenness [7], chatter [8] and arrogance [10-11].

26.6.1.en: Three things my heart fears, and for a fourth I pray.

26.6.2.en: The slander of a city, the gathering of the common people, and a false accusation: all this is heavier than death [5].

26.6.3.en: This statement is considered an introduction to his discourse on the wicked wife. Here he presents four things that cause anxiety, yet marriage to a wicked woman is more dangerous than these things.

26.6.4.en: a. The first thing is the slander of the city, or open false defamation, where a person sees injustice prevailing in the city, and there is no one who can stand before it to defend the truth.

26.6.5.en: b. The gathering of a mob, the agitation of the rabble, and the occurrence of a state of general disorder.

26.6.7.en: d. The three preceding things rest on the absence of truth and the prevalence of falsehood and vanity, which makes life tasteless, so that a person desires death, with all its heaviness, rather than life in this gloomy atmosphere. For though a person feels that he is leaving many under the yoke of injustice, it is nevertheless easier than living with the occurrence of the preceding things.

26.6.8.en: Then he moves on to the fourth grave thing, which happens in secret and not openly like the preceding things, namely a wife's jealousy of her co-wife (in polygamy) or of a woman who has a relationship with the family through kinship or neighborliness. The discourse on the wicked woman, who represents a danger more hideous than the preceding things, brings out the following:

26.6.9.en: a. The wife jealous of a woman or girl who rivals her, so that her life is turned into a whip that strikes the whole family [6].

26.7.0.en: b. The wicked wife resembles an ill-fitting yoke that makes the neck of him who bears it bleed, and a scorpion that injects venom into him who holds it [7].

26.8.0.en: c. The drunken wife exposes herself in a disgraceful shame [8].

26.9.0.en: d. The adulterous wife, even if she hides her defiled conduct, her impudent eyes bear witness to her uncleanness [9].

26.10.0.en: e. The young wife [or daughter] of little shame needs serious guarding [10].

26.11.0.en: f. The wife thirsty for defilement drinks from every water without discrimination [11-12].

26.11.1.en: There is also heartache and sorrow when a wife is jealous of another woman, and her tongue is a whip that strikes everyone [6].

26.11.2.en: This woman's heart turns into a raging volcano. For she is jealous over her husband, pursues him and suspects his conduct, whether by speaking frankly with him or in an obscure way. The tongue of the jealous woman does not keep silent, and her thought moves in a closed circle, so the house is turned into an unbearable hell. Even the children, whatever their age, lose peace and joy without knowing the hidden cause of this bitter life.

26.11.3.en: The wicked wife is like the yoke of a raging ox; he who wishes to restrain her is like one who seizes a scorpion [7].

26.11.4.en: Ben Sira compares the wicked woman to the loose yoke that moves here and there, which is placed on the neck of the ox; because it moves it causes pain, even if the ox is strong; this loose yoke affects the ox's ability to work. So the wicked woman is like a yoke on her husband's neck, causing him much pain that shatters his energy and spoils his vitality, so that she becomes like a fetter in his life, hindering his work for the sake of the family and its upbuilding. If someone intervenes to set the situation right and approaches her with wise counsel, she injects venom into him and stings him like a scorpion.

26.11.5.en: A drunken woman is a great wrath, and she does not cover her shame [8].

26.11.6.en: Evil may drive a woman to drink wine under the pretext that she forgets her cares, and since she knows no limits in drinking, she becomes drunk and loses her consciousness, as happened with Noah, who was uncovered when he got drunk. The drunken wife expresses the evils of her heart by her tongue and her conduct without balance and without prudence. She exposes the corruption of her heart and the deviation of her conduct unawares. The husband is ashamed of her behavior, especially before their children.

26.11.7.en: The adultery of the wife appears in her haughty looks and her eyelids [9].

26.11.8.en: He speaks of the impudent wicked wife, who tries to entice one who is not her husband to fall with her into sin, so she is the first one responsible for her fall and for enticing the other party. The adulterous wife denies that she has fallen into sin, but the impudence of her eyes and the movements of her eyelids bear witness against her. Solomon the wise warns against the provocative movements of her face: "Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids" (Prov 6:25). And St. Clement of Alexandria speaks of adultery through the winking of the eyes.

26.11.9.en: v No excuse can be offered for a prudent man when he sins, and still more a woman of bad repute of whatever kind, for she brings disgrace. In the words of Scripture: "A drunken woman is a great wrath, and her shame is not covered" (see Sir 26:8), for it is said of her that through wine she has become wanton and the wrath of God comes upon her. Why? Because her shameful conduct is exposed. For as soon as a woman yields to pleasure, she quickly falls into immoral acts [6].

26.11.10.en: St. Clement of Alexandria v Scripture says: "The light of the body is the eye" (Mt 6:22), for what is within is lit up, and becomes visible by the light shining upon it; therefore "the adultery of a woman is seen in the impudence of her eyes" (see Sir 26:9) [7].

26.11.11.en: St. Clement of Alexandria Keep a strict watch on the stubborn daughter, lest she find some freedom and use it to her own harm [10].

26.11.12.en: He demands wise guarding over the daughter (perhaps he means the wife of young age) who has little shame, for leniency with her in her keeping her chastity harms her. He does not ask that she be bound, but that she be supported to keep her purity. What he said about the faults of the wicked wife he sees as doubled in the case of the daughter of little shame.

26.11.13.en: Be on your guard against her shameless eye, and do not wonder if she sins against you [11].

26.11.14.en: By being on guard is meant not to go too far or be lax in speaking with her and cleaving to her. This reserve may provoke her to anger against the person, for one who has fallen into adultery cannot bear the conduct of a pure person.

26.11.15.en: Laxity in bringing up the daughter leads her to disobedience toward her father.

26.12.0.en: She opens her mouth like a thirsty traveler, and drinks from every water near her, and sits down at every tent peg, and opens her quiver to every arrow [12].

26.12.1.en: He likens the adulterous wife to an unsettled person always traveling, who suffers thirst and drinks from every water near him. For the sin of adultery makes her thirsty for every person she meets. Whenever she finds a tent peg she sits beside it to meet the one who enters the tent, so she enters with him and entices him to fall into sin.

26.13.0.en: 16 The kindness of a wife delights her husband, 17 and her discipline makes his bones fat. 18 A silent woman is a gift of the Lord, and a disciplined soul cannot be exchanged for anything. 19 A modest woman is grace upon grace. 20 And a chaste soul has no worth that can balance it. 21 The sun rises in the heights of the Lord, and the beauty of a good wife is in the order of her house. 22 The lamp shines on the holy lampstand, and a beautiful face on a sedate stature. 23 Pillars of gold stand on bases of silver, and beautiful legs on the soles of a woman of dignity. 24 Foundations on a rock stand forever, and the commandments of the Lord are in the heart of a pure woman.

26.13.1.en: After revealing the traits of the wicked wife, he tells us about the blessed wife:

26.13.2.en: a. She makes her husband glad, and makes his bones fat by her skill [13].

26.13.3.en: b. She is marked by holy silence and by conduct with good manners [14].

26.13.4.en: c. She is chaste in soul and modest in her clothing, bearing the grace of purity [15].

26.13.5.en: d. She is radiant like the sun, as one who rises from the heights of heaven [16], and she walks with management and order.

26.14.0.en: e. She gives light to those walking in darkness, like the lamp set on the lampstand [17].

26.15.0.en: f. Her movements are glorious, her feet beautiful like two pillars of gold on two bases of silver [18].

26.15.1.en: In brief, the blessed wife resembles the heavenly Jerusalem, which presents a blessed life to those who dwell in it. She also resembles the Church, the bride of Christ. Moreover, what applies to the wife, whether good or wicked, applies also to the husband, indeed to every person. In the same spirit St. Peter presents to us the role of the good wife in winning her unbelieving husband (1 Pet 3:1-5).

26.15.2.en: He began by speaking of the good, faithful, peace-loving woman as a great portion and a blessing given to him who fears the Lord [3]. After that comes his discourse on the wicked wife and the impudent daughter, and then he returns to speak of the blessed wife. It is as though he does not want the husband or father to be hasty in judging the wife or the daughter, so that he justifies to himself a revolt against them. Rather we must look to what is good and blessed in their lives, and so he begins the discourse about them and also ends it.

26.15.3.en: The traits of the good wife are:

26.15.4.en: Kindness, which pours gladness upon the husband [13].

26.15.5.en: Skill: she has her artistic and mental abilities, so she knows no sluggishness and does not fall into smallness of soul, and her husband feels as though his bones within him delight in his wife [13].

26.15.6.en: Modesty: her dignity and balance pour upon her personality grace upon grace, and her husband admires her chastity and purity [15].

26.15.7.en: Her beauty does not come from her bodily appearance, but from the splendor that shines out from her as from the sun, like a heavenly grace, and is reflected even upon the order of her house [16].

26.15.8.en: Like the lofty lampstand, she dispels the darkness and gives light to those around her.

26.15.9.en: There is harmony between the outward beauty, even of her feet, and the inward beauty of the hidden heart, which no one sees except the Lord. Her feet move upon the earth like a godly woman of God, and with her heart she soars to heaven, where the Heavenly One establishes His Kingdom in her heart. Such a wife cannot be known by anyone through his abstract thought, but she is a gift from the Lord [14].

26.15.10.en: The kindness of the wife makes her husband glad, and her skill makes his bones fat [13].

26.15.11.en: The husband sees in his blessed wife a living image of the Church, in whom the heavenly Bridegroom delights. And her skill makes his bones fat; so is the seriousness of believers in putting their skill and gifts to work for the sake of the Kingdom of God.

26.15.12.en: A silent wife is a gift from the Lord, and a disciplined soul cannot be valued at any price [14].

26.15.13.en: The wife who is silent in the Lord, her heart meditates in the law of the Lord, and her mind converses with her Savior, and her disciplined soul submits to her heavenly Bridegroom. This is reflected in the marital relationship, so that her husband feels that she cannot be valued at any price.

26.15.14.en: A modest wife is grace upon grace, and there is no scale that can weigh a chaste soul [15].

26.15.15.en: The modesty of the wife does not stop at outward appearance and clothing, but her modesty goes back to her inner life, where the Lord Himself establishes His holy and awesome Kingdom. This inner modesty is reflected in all her outward conduct, even the way she walks and her smile and her voice, so that whoever deals with her senses the overflow of God's grace upon her without interruption. He also feels a complete inability to describe her and to evaluate her life.

26.15.16.en: Like the sun rising from the heights of heaven, is the beauty of the good wife in her well-ordered house [16].

26.15.17.en: Everyone who looks at the Church of Christ sees her as an icon of the Sun of Righteousness, all light, shining upon the world and rising upon all who live in her. So the blessed wife shines like the sun from the heights of heaven. The husband and the children feel that her holy life lifts the whole house as though to Paradise. The family sees in this blessed wife that she imitates her Lord, who is not the God of confusion but of peace, as in all the churches of the saints (1 Cor 14:33).

26.15.18.en: Like the lamp that shines on the holy lampstand, is the beauty of the features in the life of one in good health [8] [17].

26.15.19.en: St. John the Beloved looked to the Lord Christ sitting on the throne with His Church around Him as seven shining lampstands (Rev 1:12). So the blessed wife, or the holy soul, is lifted by the Spirit of God, the Holy One, from glory to glory, and the heavenly ones see her as a lampstand in heaven around the divine throne.

26.15.20.en: Beautiful feet together with a steadfast heart are like pillars of gold standing on bases of silver [18].

26.15.21.en: Sirach did not describe the body of the blessed wife, but was content with her feet and her heart. The beautiful feet point to continual movement night and day, even during her slumber, as it is said: "I sleep, but my heart waketh" (Song 5:2); they move as though on the wings of the Holy Spirit from height to height, until she reaches the sight of the heavenly Bridegroom face to face (1 Cor 13:12). As for her feet, they are like pillars of gold standing on bases of silver, reminding us of the tabernacle and the temple of Solomon, which stood on pillars whose bases were silver. So the husband sees in his blessed wife the temple of God, with the Spirit of God dwelling in her (1 Cor 3:16). As for the heart, it points to the hidden heavenly sanctuaries overflowing with holiness and love.

26.16.s.en: 4. Three things that grieve the heart

26.16.0.en: 25 Two things grieve my heart, and the third makes me angry: 26 a man of war when want makes him helpless, and wise men when they are despised, 27 and one who turns back from righteousness to sin, the Lord keeps him for the sword. 28 Hardly shall a merchant be free from iniquity, and the tavern-keeper shall not be acquitted of sin.

26.16.1.en: The heart of Ben Sira grieves over two things, and anger rises in him over the third thing. What are these three things? Ben Sira feared that some young men might misunderstand his discourse on the wicked wife, and look at woman with a pessimistic eye, asking: Can a young man find a wife who has these traits? This is what led him to bring out dangerous specimens of wicked young men, such as: 1. A war hero who in his pride deviates into idleness. 2. Young men who insult the wise and despise them [19]. 3. The righteous who through their negligence deviated into sin [19]. 4. Dishonest working merchants, who commit iniquity [20] through their greed and unfaithfulness.

26.16.2.en: Two things grieve my heart, and at the third anger rises in me: a man of war who is in want because of poverty, and wise men when they are insulted, and one who turns back from righteousness to sin: the Lord will prepare him for the sword [19].

26.16.3.en: The first thing: a man of war whom poverty has made helpless. If as a man of war he exerted all his effort to protect the state, then in time of peace he must not rely on his reputation as a mighty warrior who loves his country and his people, but he must work without ceasing. Sirach looks to work as a holy matter, not only to satisfy temporal needs, but also to keep the soul striving without idleness. Therefore he demands even of the old that they work according to their ability and means.

26.16.4.en: The second thing: the insulting of the wise, instead of honoring them by imitating them and seeking their counsel.

26.16.5.en: The third thing: that a person turn back from the righteousness of God because of a temporary pleasure of sin.

26.16.6.en: v Even he who fasts for his sins, and walks in his way again and practices the same conduct, who will hear his prayer? Again we read: "If anyone turn back from his righteousness to sin, the Lord will prepare him for the sword," and also: "As a dog returneth to his vomit, so a fool returneth to his folly" (Prov 26:11) [9].

26.16.7.en: St. John Chrysostom A merchant will hardly avoid committing iniquity, and the peddler will not be acquitted of sin [20].

26.16.8.en: Trade can be a holy work when the seller and the buyer are faithful and care for the salvation of their souls.

26.16.9.en: a. The Law pointed to exactness in the balance and the measure and to not cheating.

26.16.10.en: b. Not cheating in goods offered for sale.

26.16.11.en: c. Caution against the temptation of exaggerated profit.

26.17.s.en: Prepare all as a heavenly bride!

26.17.0.en: v Every believer longs to receive his bride from Your hands.

26.17.1.en: And every believing woman wishes to see You transfigured in her bridegroom.

26.17.2.en: Let Your Holy Spirit work in every family.

26.17.3.en: Let all our life be the object of Your good pleasure and delight.

26.17.4.en: Grant us Your peace and bestow upon us Your blessings. Let our depths enjoy a foretaste of Your heavens.

26.17.5.en: And let our conduct and our features bear witness to Your grace!

26.17.6.en: v Take away from us the spirit of envy and evil jealousy, and give our tongue sweetness.

26.17.7.en: Let us be drunk with the wine of Your love, so that our heart may widen to all mankind, and our emotions and senses be sanctified by Your dwelling in us. Take away from us every deviation, and nail Your fear in us.

26.17.8.en: Grant us the single eye, not impudent. Grant me that You accompany me on the journey of my life.

26.17.9.en: So that I do not desire the waters of the world and its pleasures.

26.17.10.en: v Establish me in true membership in Your Church.

26.17.11.en: So that the heavenly ones rejoice in Your kindness to me.

26.17.12.en: And sanctify all my powers to work for Your Kingdom.

26.17.13.en: Grant me holy silence: my tongue is silent, and my heart speaks; and my heart is silent, and You, O Holy One, speak within me.

26.17.14.en: Your holy fear grants me true modesty.

26.17.15.en: It pours Your grace into me, so that my heart is filled with chastity.

26.17.16.en: v Rise, O Sun of Righteousness, from Your heavens upon my soul.

26.17.17.en: Make me a light to the world according to Your divine promise.

26.17.18.en: Let there be no place for darkness within me, but let me bear the reflection of Your splendor upon me.

26.17.19.en: v When shall I see all mankind as shining lampstands around Your throne?!

26.17.20.en: When will You light the lamp of my soul, and lift me upon the lampstand?

26.17.21.en: Sanctify even my feet, so that I move always toward Your heavens.

26.17.22.en: Count me a pillar of gold standing upon Your law, the silver base.

26.17.23.en: Grant my heart steadfastness, so that the winds of the world do not move me.

26.17.24.en: v Would that I might not grieve the hearts of the saints.

26.17.25.en: So that I may not be like an idle man of war after the battle, but work continually under the leading of Your fiery Spirit.

26.17.26.en: And that I may not despise the wise, but seek their counsel, their prayers and their blessing.

26.17.27.en: And that I may not return to sin again, but hide in Your righteousness.

26.17.28.en: v Make me a faithful merchant, who does not covet the possessions of the world, nor walk in a spirit of deceit, but sells everything in order to acquire You.

26.17.29.en: O You, the Pearl of great price!
